summary: PLATE 0.8.4 -- babysit --watch backs off and enforces spend caps. Cheap PR change detection and delta wake summaries ship as libraries for the watcher.

entries.migration_impact: No downstream repo migration. Watch integration lands in a follow-up PR; this release only adds the pure summary module and agent wiki guidance.
entries.agent_notes: On babysit watch wake, call build_wake_summary with REST deltas and prev/cur snapshots. Act on render_wake_summary output when is_actionable is true. Do not poll _load_pr_data every tick; reload full PR state only when the summary indicates merge conflict or insufficient detail.
migration_guidance: 1. Upgrade plate-core when the release containing #1080 ships.
2. On wake, prefer build_wake_summary/render_wake_summary over full GraphQL PR reload unless merge conflict or missing detail requires it.
3. Read docs/wiki/PR-Babysit-Wake-Summary.md for agent operating rules.

entries.migration_impact: No downstream migration until a follow-up PR wires the probe into gh plate pr babysit --watch. Libraries may import plate_core.pr_watch_probe for cheap change detection.
entries.agent_notes: Use probe_pr with an injected or GhApiHttp client; a 304 avoids reloading the PR resource, while commit status and check runs are polled each probe. Persist ProbeState under .agentic/babysit/<owner>-<repo>-<pr>.probe.json. fetch_delta loads only new comments and reviews since last_checked_at.
migration_guidance: 1. Upgrade plate-core when this ships on the release track.
2. Babysit --watch behavior is unchanged until the watch loop integration lands in a later Epic #1077 slice.

entries.migration_impact: No downstream action required. Existing --interval remains supported as a deprecated alias for --min-interval.
entries.agent_notes: The --watch loop uses exponential backoff, resetting when the babysit report changes, and stops on merge, close, or --max-hours. The watcher always removes its pidfile on exit.
migration_guidance: 1. Use --min-interval and --max-interval to configure polling backoff.
2. Use --max-hours to stop a watch after a wall-clock duration.

entries.migration_impact: No repository migration. Watch loops use local cap ledgers under .agentic/babysit/ and pause when either spend cap is reached.
entries.agent_notes: Babysit watch caps are enforced before and after each poll. Pass --max-wakes and --cap-hours to change the defaults. A cap pause posts at most one PR comment containing <!-- plate-babysit-cap -->. The ledger records cap_note_posted, and a later pause still searches newer comment pages for that marker. The --status option reports saved wake and elapsed-hour usage. A human must explicitly pass --reset-caps to start a new budget. Cap ledger filenames are length-prefixed so owner/name pairs that share a hyphenated slug do not share a budget.
migration_guidance: 1. Upgrade plate-core to the release that contains watch cap integration.
2. Inspect saved usage with `gh plate pr babysit <n> --status`.
4. After a cap pause, start a new budget with `gh plate pr babysit <n> --watch --reset-caps`.
